decisions.summary: Commit the C1 to a single, option-light trim at a $36,900 starting price rather than a laddered trim lineup.
decisions.rationale: Affordable is the product. A single trim collapses build complexity, speeds the ramp, and keeps the price below the segment ceiling set by the Chevy Equinox EV and a tariff-gated BYD. Trim sprawl would erode the one advantage we have.
decisions.outcome: C1 ships as one trim with a short options list. Marketing positions on total cost of ownership vs. the Model Y.

decisions.summary: Adopt LFP cell chemistry for the C1 and begin qualifying a second cell source beyond CATL.
decisions.rationale: LFP wins on cost and cycle life for a value buyer who cares about longevity over peak range. But single-sourcing cells from CATL is both a supply risk and a tariff/policy risk. We need a second qualified source before we ramp to 4,000/month.
decisions.outcome: LFP locked for C1. Operations opened second-source qualification with Panasonic and LG Energy Solution; still in progress.

decisions.summary: Ship the C1 NACS-native so buyers get Tesla Supercharger access from day one.
decisions.rationale: Charging access is the top stated anxiety for our first-time-EV target customer. NACS-native removes the adapter friction and lets marketing make a clean Supercharger-access claim against incumbents still transitioning.
decisions.outcome: C1 ships with a NACS port. Polestar and Ford comparisons used in the charging narrative.

decisions.summary: Hold C1 pricing flat through the next Tesla Model Y price cut rather than reflexively matching it.
decisions.rationale: Matching every Tesla cut torches the path to gross-margin-positive, which is the north-star metric this year. We compete on total cost of ownership and Supercharger access, not on headline price wars we cannot afford pre-margin.
decisions.outcome: Pricing held. Strategy to publish a TCO comparison instead of cutting. Flagged for same-day review if a cut is paired with a 30D credit change.

initiatives.title: C1 production ramp to 4,000 units/month
initiatives.summary: Lift line throughput from 2,600 to 4,000 vehicles/month to clear the 31K-unit backlog. Gated on second-source LFP cell qualification and quality holds; owned by Operations (Chris).

initiatives.title: Path to gross-margin-positive per vehicle
initiatives.summary: Move gross margin per vehicle from -6% toward breakeven before the next raise — via bill-of-materials cost-downs, ramp-driven fixed-cost absorption, and pricing discipline against Tesla cuts. Owned by Finance (Sam).

initiatives.title: Second-source LFP cell qualification
initiatives.summary: Retire single-source CATL exposure by qualifying a second LFP cell supplier (Panasonic / LG Energy Solution). Tied to both supply resilience and IRA Section 30D sourcing eligibility. Owned by Operations with Legal review.

initiatives.title: Affordable-EV TCO marketing narrative
initiatives.summary: Publish a transparent total-cost-of-ownership story against the Tesla Model Y and Chevy Equinox EV — including NACS Supercharger access — to convert range-anxious first-time EV buyers without cutting price. Owned by Marketing (Morgan).

initiatives.title: C2 sedan platform build-vs-defer decision
initiatives.summary: Decide whether to greenlight the C2 sedan on the next platform now or defer until C1 hits gross-margin-positive. Board decision memo in progress. Owned by Product (Jordan) with Finance and Strategy input.

initiatives.title: Ramp-critical hiring plan
initiatives.summary: Fill 40 ramp-critical manufacturing and quality roles in a competitive EV talent market without overpaying into a bidding war. Watch competitor layoffs/hiring freezes for talent availability. Owned by People (Morgan).

advice_given.query_summary: Should we match the latest Tesla Model Y price cut?
advice_given.advice_summary: Hold C1 pricing and publish a transparent TCO + Supercharger-access comparison instead. Matching every Tesla cut torches the path to gross-margin-positive, which is this year's north-star. Flag for same-day review only if a cut is paired with a 30D credit change.

advice_given.query_summary: How urgent is qualifying a second LFP cell source?
advice_given.advice_summary: Treat it as gating for both the 4,000/month ramp and 30D sourcing eligibility. Qualify Panasonic/LG before scaling — single-source CATL is simultaneously a supply risk and a tariff/policy risk.

scheduled_actions.intent_text: Starting from a clean baseline: research the landscape across all specialists and propose what we should be watching — add the highest-signal sources to the watchlist. Web-search current moves by Tesla, Rivian, Lucid, BYD, Ford, GM, and Hyundai/Kia; EV tax-credit (IRA 30D) and tariff changes; battery-supplier (CATL, Panasonic, LG Energy Solution) and NHTSA recall signals. Propose watchlist additions for the most decision-relevant signals, and only route something to a department head if it is genuinely urgent.
